previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and a history of recurrent urinary tract infections due to resistant organisms, was admitted after being found lethargic at home with high fever, chills, and weakness. He was diagnosed with severe sepsis secondary to an ESBL-producing E. coli infection originating from the urinary tract, with bacteremia and acute kidney injury. He responded well to fluid resuscitation and intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam, with normalization of lactate, kidney function, and clinical status. A PICC line was placed to complete a full course of IV antibiotics at a rehabilitation facility. His chronic left hip wound, sustained from a fall, was monitored but not considered infected. He was discharged to extended care with plans for wound care, antibiotic completion, and follow-up with his primary care and specialty providers.
problems: Septicemia due to escherichia coli [E. coli]
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Posttraumatic wound infection not elsewhere classified

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

Comparison is made with a prior study from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ man with fever and chills as well as shortness
of breath x2-3 days, question pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  AP supine portable view of the chest was obtained.  Evaluation is
limited given the partial exclusion of the left lower chest.  The patient is
slightly rotated to the left, also limiting evaluation somewhat.  Hardware
along the lower cervical spine is again noted.  The imaged portions of the
lungs appear clear.  There is unchanged appearance of an ovoid dense nodule in
the right lower lung which likely represents a calcified granuloma.  There may
also be a similar left mid lung calcified granuloma, also unchanged.  There is
no evidence of pneumonia or CHF.  No large pleural effusion or pneumothorax is
seen.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of pneumonia.  Somewhat limited study.

PORTABLE SUPINE AP VIEW OF THE CHEST

Comparison is made with a prior study from approximately two hours earlier.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Fever, elevated lactate, status post right IJ central line
placement, question position of catheter.

FINDINGS:  Single AP portable supine view of the chest is obtained with
exclusion of the lateral lower right chest.  There has been interval placement
of a right IJ central venous catheter with its tip positioned appropriately in
the expected location of the superior vena cava.  The lungs remain clear
bilaterally with areas of calcified nodularity again noted in the left and
right lungs.  There is no pneumothorax or new lung opacity.

IMPRESSION:  Appropriate position of right IJ central venous catheter.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ male with fever and tachycardia.  Evaluate
baclofen pump.

TECHNIQUE:  Single AP radiograph of the abdomen and pelvis was obtained with
the patient in the supine position.

FINDINGS:  There is a normal bowel gas pattern without dilation or air-fluid
levels.  Stool is seen in the descending colon and rectum.  There is no
pneumatosis.  This exam is not optimized for evaluation for free air.

A hardware device is seen overlying the lateral left lower quadrant.  A thin
catheter appears to be traversing from this hardware over the left lower
quadrant, meeting the region of the spine at the L3-L4 intervertebral level,
and following the course of the spine in the superior direction overlying the
midline.  The tip of this catheter is not visualized.  Surgical clips are seen
overlying the region of the left pelvis.  

Mild bony degenerative changes are seen.

IMPRESSION:  External hardware which likely represents the patient's baclofen
pump with catheter traversing superiorly overlying the spine in the midline.

INDICATION:  ___ man with recurrent UTI.

COMPARISON:  ___.

SINGLE SEMI-UPRIGHT VIEW OF THE CHEST AT 14:05 HOURS:  A right internal
jugular catheter terminates in the SVC, unchanged.  Lung volumes are low,
resulting in vascular crowding.  There is no consolidation or pleural
effusion.  There is no pneumothorax.  The heart size is unchanged.  Previously
noted lung nodules, likely granulomas, are unchanged bilaterally.

Fixation hardware in the cervical spine is stable, although incompletely
imaged.

IMPRESSION:  Low lung volumes, without acute abnormality.

HIP THREE VIEWS.

REASON FOR EXAM:  Chronic ulcer.  Evaluate for osteomyelitis.

There is no evidence of fracture, dislocation, osteoblastic or osteolytic
osseous lesions. There are mild degenerative changes in the hip joints
bilaterally.  There are multiple surgical staples and clips along the anterior
portion of the left hemipelvis.  There is increase of stool in the rectum.

IMPRESSION:  No radiographic evidence for osteomyelitis.  If continued
clinical concern for a bone infection, further evaluation with MRI is
recommended.

CHEST ON ___

HISTORY:  Shortness of breath, leukocytosis.

REFERENCE EXAM:  ___.

FINDINGS:  The right IJ line tip is in the SVC.  There is some subsegmental
atelectasis in both lower lungs.  There is no definite infiltrate.

PROCEDURE:  Placement of right-sided midline venous catheter.

HISTORY:  ___ man requires IV access for antibiotic therapy.

ANESTHESIA:  1% lidocaine was administered to the skin over the venipuncture
site.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ performed the
procedure.  Dr. ___, the attending radiologist, supervised the
procedure.

PROCEDURE:  Informed verbal consent was obtained outlining the risks and
benefits of the procedure involved.  Following administration of local
anesthetic, the right basilic vein was accessed with a micropuncture needle. 
A guide wire was passed to the level of the upper basilic vein, but was not
advanced further.  A 5 ___ peel-away sheath was advanced over the wire. 
Contrast was injected demonstrating venous stenosis in the region of the mid
basilic vein.  A 0.018 Glidewire was successfully passed through the stenosis
into the SVC; however, we could not advance the catheter over the wire.
Following discussion with the team, decision was made to place a midline
catheter only to allow antibiotic infusion.  The catheter was cut to 11 cm
with its tip positioned in the upper basilic vein.

IMPRESSION:  Venous stenosis in the upper basilic vein which prevented passage
of the 4 ___ single lumen catheter, despite passage of the Glidewire. 
Given that the patient does not require central access, the team was happy
with placement of a long line and an 11-cm catheter was placed with the tip
terminating in the mid/upper right basilic vein.  The catheter may be used
immediately.

The staff radiologist has reviewed the report.
